newsitem.title: MAURITANIA: Mauritania frees politicians held over Libya links.
newsitem.headline: Mauritania frees politicians held over Libya links.

text.p: The Mauritanian authorities have freed the head of the main opposition Action for Change party after holding him on accusations of suspect relations with Libya, his family said on Thursday.

Messoud ould Boulkheir, whose party won the first and only opposition seat in October's parliamentary election, was arrested with three other politicians on January 22. He began a hunger strike on Tuesday and was released overnight Wednesday.

The others held were Abdallahi el Atigh ould Yahi, spokesman for a group opposing normalisation with Israel, El Khory ould Hmeity, former general-secretary of the Mauritanian workers union, and Hamoud ould Abdi, a member of the national committee of the ruling Democratic and Social Republican Party.
Sources close to Hmeity said he too had been released.
Mauritania's relations with Libya, shunned by the West on suspicion of terrorism links, are traditionally strained, with Nouakchott accusing Tripoli of trying to destabilise it.
Mauritania more commonly cracks down on individuals for ties with Iraq, a country with which it traditionally enjoyed close ties until changing tack after the 1991 Gulf war over Kuwait.
President Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya and his ruling party won a landslide victory in October's parliamentary election.

Action for Change is a new party championing the rights of Mauritania's blacks and ex-slaves. Moors of Arab stock traditionally dominate the government of the former French colony, which straddles black and Arab Africa.
